entry.evidence: the chemical data comparable to that on the modern deposits of various occurrences are almost lacking

steps.action: Name a gap: Green Tuff bedded Mn deposits lack chemical data comparable to modern deposits, and the associated iron ores have not been treated systematically.
steps.quote: the chemical data comparable to that on the modern deposits of various occurrences are almost lacking

steps.action: Take the stratigraphic setting and radiolarian age of the deposits from the authors' earlier work (Sakai et al. 2019), which reassigns them to the Odoji formation and implies a hiatus of more than 6 Myr.
steps.quote: Sakai et al. (2019) reports the radiolarian age of the manganese ores from Kitaichi deposit in this area

steps.action: Sample three deposits (Kitaichi, Teranosawa, Maruyama), classify the ores into lower goethite and upper todorokite ore, and identify minerals by optical microscopy, XRD and SEM-EDS.
steps.quote: The ores are lithologically classified into two, that is, lower goethite ore and upper todorokite ore.

steps.action: Calibrate the XRF analyses against GSJ rock standards, their composites and element-doped variants, and cite earlier work for the accuracies.
steps.quote: Analyses were calibrated using the Geological Survey of Japan (GSJ) rock standards and their composites

steps.action: Report XRF major- and trace-element compositions for ores and host sandstones and identify the elements enriched in each ore type.
steps.quote: The ores in the bedded manganese deposits are high in certain elements

steps.action: Establish a vertical compositional zoning in the Kitaichi profile from the concentration profiles (Fe-As-Y, P-Pb, Cu, Co-W-Tl, Mn-Ba-Mo-Sr-V in ascending order).
steps.quote: There is distinct compositional zoning in the Kitaichi

steps.action: Plot the data on the published Fe-Mn-(Cu+Ni+Zn) discrimination diagram; the data fall in the hydrothermal and suboxic diagenetic fields.
steps.quote: Fukaura data are plotted in the hydrothermal region, and many manganese ore also in suboxic diagenetic region

steps.action: Propose an early diagenetic redistribution model (Figure 6): Mn is reduced, migrates and redeposits upward, Fe stays behind as residual goethite, and the hiatus preserves the profile.
steps.quote: Separation of manganese from iron would lead to forming a clear set of lower goethite and upper todorokite ores.

steps.action: Cite an analogous stratigraphic Mn/Fe separation in buried nodules from the Clarion-Clipperton Zone (Heller et al. 2018).
steps.quote: they described stratigraphic separation of upper migrated manganese with high Cu and Ni contents from lower residual iron

steps.action: Hypothesize that the zoning reflects the different adsorption of cations and oxyanions on Mn versus Fe oxyhydroxides, which have opposite surface charge (ZPC).
steps.quote: Absorption properties of manganese oxyhydroxides are known to be different from those of iron oxyhydroxides

steps.action: Compare the enriched elements of each ore with the charge of their dominant seawater species (Byrne 2002); cations match todorokite and anions match goethite, except W, Mo and V.
steps.quote: it is clearly shown that positive species found in todorokite, while negative in goethite

steps.action: Explain the W, Mo and V mismatch by Eh-dependent ligand changes or inner/outer-sphere complexation (Kashiwabara et al. 2013), rather than revise the adsorption hypothesis.
steps.quote: The reason is not clear now, but Eh conditions would be possible to change the complex ligands of these elements.

steps.action: Conclude that the heavy-metal zoning is basically caused by differential adsorption on goethite and todorokite during early diagenetic redistribution.
steps.quote: The zoning of heavy metals in bedded manganese deposits from the Fukaura area is concluded to be basically caused by differences in adsorption properties

steps.action: Reconstruct the original (pre-diagenetic) composition by averaging goethite and todorokite ores for each deposit.
steps.quote: reconstructed original chemical composition representative of three bedded manganese deposits

steps.action: Compare the reconstructed compositions with modern ferromanganese deposits (Figure 7); they resemble hydrothermal and suboxic diagenetic deposits, not hydrogenous or oxic diagenetic ones.
steps.quote: The compositions are not similar to those of hydrogenous and oxic diagenetic ferromanganese deposits

steps.action: State two rival sources for the primary Fe-Mn deposit: submarine hydrothermal activity, or upwelling of anoxic stratified water (bathtub-ring type).
steps.quote: We should keep in mind the possibility of submarine hydrothermal

steps.action: Keep both source candidates and defer the choice between them, including possible combined factors, to future research.
steps.quote: Further research will be needed to determine which of the above two is more appropriate

steps.action: Report that the lower goethite / upper todorokite division recurs at a second deposit (Teranosawa) as well as Kitaichi.
steps.quote: The bedded manganese deposit is clearly divided into lower goethite and upper todorokite ores at the Kitaichi and Teranosawa Mines

tree.answer: Three deposits; ore division recurs at two
Partly; W, Mo, V contradict the ZPC rule

end.claim: The goethite-todorokite separation and the compositional zoning of the Fukaura bedded Mn deposits arise from early diagenetic redistribution of Mn and differential adsorption on goethite and todorokite.

decisive_move.sentence: Establishing the vertical compositional zoning in the Kitaichi profile is the phenomenon that the diagenesis and adsorption model is built to explain.

gates.evidence: Sampling and analysis were descriptive; the diagenetic model is introduced only in the Discussion (p. 7). The comparison with seawater speciation could fail and partly did (W, Mo, V; p. 8), but the authors protected the model. They state the model's validity 'has to wait for future research' (p. 9). Nothing was fixed in advance.

imports.item: zero-point charge of oxyhydroxide surfaces (Stumm & Morgan 1996)
X-ray fluorescence, XRD and SEM-EDS analysis
XAFS and micro-XRF mapping (cited, Kashiwabara et al. 2013)

novelty_claims.quote: the iron ores associated with manganese ores have not been treated comprehensively and systematically in this region

limits: The diagenetic model and the adsorption explanation are qualitative and never tested quantitatively; the authors say validity 'has to wait for future research' (p. 9). The full element zoning is shown only for the Kitaichi profile; Teranosawa replicates the ore division, but Maruyama has only todorokite ore. The original composition is assumed to be a simple average of the two ores, with no alternative tested. The source of the primary deposit (hydrothermal vs anoxic upwelling) stays at no conclusion. The data sub-claim (compositions and enrichments) is an observation with cited, not newly reported, analytical accuracy. Two anonymous reviewers are acknowledged, but no review file was supplied, so changes made in review are unknown (inference). Data are available only on request.

disagreements.support: Adopts the radiolarian ages of Sakai et al. (2019), which place the deposits in the Odoji formation of the Onnagawa stage.
disagreements.quote: Recently, however, Sakai et al. (2019) reports the radiolarian age of the manganese ores from Kitaichi deposit

disagreements.target: Yamada et al. (2012); Yamada & Yoshida (2004): Onnagawa period of inactive magmatism
disagreements.support: The hydrothermal-type chemical signature (Figures 4, 7) and the tuffaceous footwall suggest hydrothermal input despite inactive magmatism.
disagreements.quote: However, the chemical composition of the Fukaura manganese deposits have the characteristics of hydrothermal origin

disagreements.target: Generally accepted origin by submarine magmatic exhalation (Moritani 1964; Yoshimura 1952)
disagreements.support: Offers upwelling of anoxic stratified water as an alternative source, by analogy with bathtub-ring deposits.
disagreements.quote: On the other hand, it is also necessary to emphasize the formation of the anaerobic basin

alternatives_considered.alternatives: submarine hydrothermal activity; upwelling of anoxic stratified water; combined factors
